name: Lands of the Engineers
description: The home islands of the [[Engineers]], the unnamed empire: [[Inis Tíre]] and [[Inis Mara]]. Strictly, their own territory is Inis Tíre and [[Sail]]; the rest of Inis Mara they oversee, though three of its provinces are nominally held by others, like embassy land. In the projection: the United Kingdom and Ireland.

name: Lands of the Sapphire Throne
description: The realm of the [[Sapphire Kingdom]]. In the projection: Yemen, Djibouti and Eritrea.

name: Lands of the Eastern Emirates
description: The lands of the [[Eastern Emirates]]. In the projection: Morocco, Mauritania, Senegal, Gambia, Algeria and Tunisia.

name: Lands of the Threefold Republic
description: The lands of the [[Threefold Republic]]. In the projection: Sudan, Chad, the Central African Republic, Cameroon, Nigeria and Benin.

name: Lands of the Elven Islands
description: The islands of the [[Elven Islands]]. In the projection: Madagascar and Malaysia. Madagascar lies close to the globe's north pole, so it is drawn much stretched.

name: Lands of the Dragon Seat
description: The islands of the [[Dragon Seat]]. In the projection: Indonesia.

name: Lands of the Empire of the Sun
description: The continent over which the [[Empire of the Sun]] has jurisdiction, as foreign powers see it. In the projection: North and Central America, with the Caribbean. Its barely habitable interior is in practice held by indigenous tribes, the [[Sandfolk]], whose control the Empire does not recognise.

name: Lands of the Sandfolk
description: The barely habitable interior of the continent, held in practice by the indigenous tribes of the [[Sandfolk]], though the [[Empire of the Sun]] claims it and does not recognise their control. In the projection: the US Midwest.

name: Lands of the Tribes of Hanathy
description: The lands of the [[Tribes of Hanathy]]. In the projection: South America.

name: Lands of the Keepers of Mantra
description: The islands of the [[Keepers of Mantra]]. In the projection: Svalbard.
The continent of the Six Kingdoms and the Nine States, also called the Great Lands.

Farming country of the High Marks, including the Western Dells, which the Engineers treat as their own. Farm produce is its main export; rural communities resist foreign influence. Terrain die 2.

- **[[rolltable/setting-seeds-culture-table|Culture]]: Scholarly Conquest.** The [[Engineers]] have quietly colonised the land around the [[Black Dunes|black-sand dunes]] and the [[Ancient Channel|ancient channels]], extracting vast amounts of valuable materials and learning, while the native people of the Dells carry on their lives in the more fertile land around them.
- **[[rolltable/setting-seeds-resources-table|Resources]]: Much Ore, Little Land.**

Volcanic sands, highly rich in ore, once sacred land to the [[True Church]]. The [[Engineers]] have claimed them. Terrain die 4.

On the world globe (pole 50.27°E 10°S, seam 150°E 50°S, south compression 0.5, E/W 0.55), remapped Burgas sits at about 27.4°N 10.6°W. The globe is tilted: climate follows a hot axis, not in-world latitude, and measured from that axis this area sits at a climate latitude of about 46°, much colder than its 27°N suggests. That makes it cold, at the edge of the ice belt, and moderately dry, since much of what lies within 8° is land. On the globe's overlay it reads as pale, cold steppe or moorland, partly whitened by ice. Real east now points west-north-west here, so the real Black Sea coast faces west. Physically, think of the Kamchatka Peninsula: volcanoes, glaciers and black volcanic sand, though drier.
A landmark in the mountains north-east of Hearth.
A stone aqueduct bridge over the river beside the trading post, now its crossing.

name: The Leantain Reach
description: A march in the Leantain west, held by [[Lord Read of the Leantain Reach|Lord Read]].

name: The Prime Reach
description: The [[Engineers]]' first canal in the [[Greater Lands]], across Zintar from the [[Inner Sea]] to the [[Bay of Brael]], bypassing the [[Freti]]; with the strip on either side, the territory of the [[Committee Exterior]]. In the projection: the Kiel Canal.

name: Inis Mara
description:
The sparsely settled island beside [[Inis Tíre]]. The whole island is overseen by the [[Engineers]], and Sail is strictly theirs; the other three provinces are nominally held by others, like embassy land, as diplomatic domains under the Engineers' protection: [[Luis]] the preserve of [[the Nine States]], [[Fern]] of [[the Six Kingdoms]], [[Beth]] nominally of [[the Empire of the Sun]], while [[Sail]] is the unnamed empire's own, administered directly by the [[Committee Interior]]. Outside [[Ephemeristorum]] its people are the island's own. The ports are run by, and matter to, the governments that nominally hold them, each through a joint mandate: boards and committees, such as the [[Diplomatic Board of the Six Kingdoms]], that mostly work outside the machinations of mainland politics, keeping to the mundane decisions while local communities manage the affairs of daily life. The trade in technologically advanced goods is too essential to risk, so all who take part keep their business here mercantile, not political. Strictly, importing through these lands is the only way outside powers may deal with the Committee Interior. In the projection: Ireland.

Its nominal provinces date from [[the Division of Inis Mara]], after centuries in which the [[Empire of the Sun]] invaded it again and again ([[event/the-coming|history]]).

name: Luis
description: The province of [[Inis Mara]] nominally held by [[the Nine States]] as their diplomatic domain, like embassy land, under the [[Engineers]]' oversight and protection. In the projection: Leinster.

name: Fern
description: The province of [[Inis Mara]] nominally held by [[the Six Kingdoms]] as their diplomatic domain, like embassy land, under the [[Engineers]]' oversight and protection. In the projection: Connacht.

name: Beth
description: The province of [[Inis Mara]] nominally held by [[the Empire of the Sun]] as its diplomatic domain, like embassy land, under the [[Engineers]]' oversight and protection, though the Empire has never been in functional diplomatic relations with the unnamed empire. In the projection: Munster.

name: Sail
description: The province of [[Inis Mara]] that is strictly the unnamed empire's own territory, administered directly by the [[Committee Interior]]. Home to [[Ephemeristorum]]. In the projection: Ulster.

name: Ephemeristorum
description: The most famous city of the [[Engineers]], at the head of its lough, a fortress city on an island laid out like a yin-yang: ringed by the [[Orbital]], a moat some 500 m wide dug against the [[Empire of the Sun]], and divided by the narrow [[Serpentine]] into [[Ephe]] and [[Stora]]. Beyond the Orbital is [[the Verge]], dense city with inhabitants and traders of every nation. Some 150,000 to 200,000 people live in the whole, about as many as in Amsterdam at the end of the 18th century: some 30,000 in Ephe, perhaps 10,000 in Stora, and the rest in the Verge. By strict law and capital decree no citizen of the unnamed empire may leave it, or treat with those outside, except as a member of a body under the [[Committee Exterior]]; Ephemeristorum is the only place exempt, and so the one place a realm can negotiate with the [[Committee Interior]] directly, and lobby beyond the reach of the [[Committee Exterior]]. By these means the committees keep a tight control of knowledge and discovery: for if knowledge lives in heads, then those who leave must leave their heads behind. In the projection: Belfast, at the head of Belfast Lough.

name: The Orbital
description: The moat of [[Ephemeristorum]]: a ring of water some 500 m wide about the island of [[Ephe]] and [[Stora]]. It was dug when the islanders fell back to Ephe before the [[Empire of the Sun]], to hold the Empire's raids off the walls until relief came from [[Inis Tíre]], and has been tidied since into a canal, its inner bank the island's bastioned walls and its outer the Verge's quays. Along its outer bank hulks lie moored, floating bonded stores of goods awaiting their clearance. Nothing crosses it unbidden: Ephe has no way over it but by water, and Stora three causeways to [[the Verge]], each with a gatehouse at either end and a hydraulic swing span that is swung open to shut it. Its water is the river's own, held level above the weir; below the weir the [[Lagan Estuary]] is tidal, and a lock with hydraulic gates through the Orbital's outer bank joins the estuary's pool to the moat: the only way in by water.

name: The Serpentine
description: The narrow canal winding across the island within the [[Orbital]], dividing [[Ephe]] from [[Stora]]. Two bridges cross it, over which only approved envoys from among the unnamed empire's own inhabitants may pass; beneath the water a deep fence bars any other way across. No one not native to the empire may ever enter Ephe.

name: Ephe
description:
The half of [[Ephemeristorum]] within the [[Orbital]] that is the exclusive preserve of the inhabitants of the unnamed empire, which no one not native to it may ever enter: a walled city on a steep rocky mound, peaking at the [[Exarch's Palace]], much like Edinburgh's Old Town in its closes and its crowding, and about its size: some 30,000 people in less than half a square kilometre, its bastioned walls rising from the moat. It runs on steam and hydraulic power alone. Here wealth grows to its peak; but at its very base, beneath the eye of its polished surface, is a network of steamy, rusty caverns and tunnels where the impoverished and menial labourers dwell. Its only ways in are its north-west-facing port on the Orbital, which ships from [[Inis Tíre]] reach from the estuary through the Orbital's lock without touching any other land: a quay cut into the foot of the Hill's tail, where hydraulic cranes work the ships and lifts and water-balance funiculars climb the wall behind it to the city above; and the two bridges over the [[Serpentine]], which only the empire's own approved envoys may cross.

It survived [[the Siege of Ephe]] behind its walls.

Ephe was a city that thrust to the heavens, a star ascending above the foundations of its bosom brothers, rising on an airstream of modernity - severe edifices of classical bearing, cut sharp like a miser's whiskers; brick pragmatists, like fixated alchemists, discretion lost in a maze of chimneys, eaves and chutes, and jutting tufts of wood and wire: and at its crest, wide, steep streets, groomed as a dowager duchess, wealth in every polished stone, stucco frontage and heraldic crest wrought through iron railings like soldiers of a new metallic era.

name: Stora
description: The other half of [[Ephemeristorum]] within the [[Orbital]]: the only place in the world where approved delegates of other nations can meet those on the business of the [[Committee Interior]], and even the [[Imperial Academy of Scientific Endeavour]], the [[Ancient Universities]] and the [[Merchant Leagues]], who lead research and trade within the unnamed empire. Scrutiny is close, but it is a unique diplomatic oasis: the elite hub of the city, a little like Buda's castle quarter, and like it unable to grow within its bounds. Some 10,000 live there, the delegations and their households among quarters older than the order that keeps them: a harbourside by its port, quarters of alleys and blind lanes, courtyard houses, gardens crammed in and misfit chapels, halls and towers, as in Jerusalem's old city or an old port like Bristol, and about the Delegates' Hall at the head of the Avenue the walled compounds of the delegations. Reached only by three causeways across the Orbital from the Verge, each shut by swinging open its span, and its own south-east-facing port on the Orbital.

name: The Exarch's Palace
description:
The grand palace at the peak of [[Ephe]], seat of the [[Exarch of Ephe]]: a Greek cross, much as Palladio's Rotonda is, at the scale of Stormont, with a portico of fluted columns on each of its four arms, one facing the forecourt at the head of the Spine, and parterres in the corners between them.

But above it all, the Hill was capped by the Palace - an enormous villa of hundreds of rooms, the stately home of an august aesthete, airy and grand in its tan clunch, with fortitude in every stony fluted column. It gave the imagination to wonder of a story, where a wealthy giant whose hubris led him to ignore the land beneath his feet, built his mansion on a mountain peak, as though he might walk on air.

name: Inis Tíre
description: The greater of the home islands of the [[Engineers]], beside [[Inis Mara]]. In the projection: Great Britain.

name: The Upper Reaches
description: The [[Engineers]]' canals of [[place/high-marks|the High Marks]] and further north and east, kept for the [[Committee Exterior]] by its Warden.

name: The Inselberg of the God-Kings
description: The Olympus-like inselberg where, in the old legends, the [[God-Kings]] had their capital. Its place is unknown.

name: Ruiata
description: The capital of [[group/realm-miurna|Miurna]], on the flat top of the [[Tor Ruiait]].

name: The Northern Elven Islands
description: The polar islands of the northern elves of the [[Elven Islands]], unseen by humans for a millennium. In the projection: Madagascar.

name: The Southern Elven Islands
description: The islands of the southern elves of the [[Elven Islands]]. In the projection: Malaysia.

name: The Verge
description: The city of [[Ephemeristorum]] beyond the [[Orbital]], with inhabitants and traders of every nation: dense and canal-laced, much like Amsterdam at the end of the 18th century. The cut-off, poorer sibling of [[Ephe]] and [[Stora]], but with no natural enemies and free to sprawl, and its port industry makes it the best-connected free city in the world. Its trade is uniquely with the [[Committee Interior]] itself, as foreigners once traded with China only at Canton's factories, and laid out as Amsterdam's staple market was: goods held in store until the price is right. Its wealth gathers at two poles. At [[the Docks]] and the Orbital's lock lie the Committee Interior's goods in bulk, in bond until declassified and dealt for, and the poor who work them; at [[the Gates]], where Stora's causeways land, the negotiators, brokers and agents who deal for them, and the small, dear goods released through [[Stora]]. Between, [[the Rings]] are richest near the Gates; beyond them, by the docks, the poorest quarters crowd, and the dirty trades that work up what is landed (sugar, spirits, soap, dye, rope, tobacco) keep to the north-east, downwind. Far from everywhere, it is the one place all the nations and merchants of the [[Greater Lands]] are guaranteed to trade in peace, perpetually.

Ephe's lifeline to [[Inis Tíre]]: the tidal channel of the Lagan, deep enough for ships, from the head of the lough up to Ephe's port at the Orbital's break, widening below the weir into a pool where ships can turn. For the 1.5 km it runs through [[the Verge]], the Engineers wall both its banks, so that it is Ephe's water and ships pass between the foreign quays without touching them; at night they close its mouth with a boom, as the deep fence closes the [[Serpentine]].

name: The Crag
description: The palace precinct on the top of the [[Hill]]'s crag, at the head of the Spine, the street that runs down the crag's tail to the quay: the [[Exarch's Palace]], its forecourt, and the houses of the empire's greatest, looking down over the walls on every side. Wide, steep streets fall from it, groomed as a dowager duchess: wealth in every polished stone, stucco frontage and heraldic crests wrought through iron railings. Ephe's wealth at its peak.

name: The Closes
description: The slopes of [[Ephe]] off the Spine, the street that runs down the [[Hill]]'s tail from the palace to the quay: narrow closes and steps dropping off both sides between lands, tenements ten storeys and more, much like Edinburgh's Old Town: severe edifices of classical bearing, cut sharp like a miser's whiskers, on the Spine, and behind them brick pragmatists, their discretion lost in a maze of chimneys, eaves and chutes and jutting tufts of wood and wire. Rich and poor live stacked in the same lands, the better floors in the middle, the poorer at the top and in the cellars.

name: Ephe's Quay
description: Ephe's harbour: the quay cut into the foot of the [[Hill]]'s tail on the [[Orbital]], under a high wall. Ships from [[Inis Tíre]] come to it from the [[Lagan Estuary]]'s pool through the lock in the Orbital's outer bank, and across the moat; hydraulic cranes work them; an accumulator holds the mains at pressure; and two water-balance funiculars climb the wall to the Spine. Here too goods for a particular deal come in small batches for the empire's inspection, to be released through [[Stora]].

name: The Undercity
description: Beneath all of [[Ephe]]'s polished surface: the steamy, rusty caverns and tunnels where the impoverished and menial labourers dwell, and the plant that runs the city above, its boilers, pumps and hydraulic mains. Its passages run under the closes and round the foot of the crag.

name: The Old Verge
description: The oldest of [[the Verge]], round the [[Orbital]]: crowded streets of every nation between the road round the Orbital and the first ring canal.

name: The Rings
description: The ring canals of [[the Verge]], horseshoes opening onto the lough much as Amsterdam's open onto the IJ, lined with the tall, narrow houses and warehouses of its merchants: the Verge at its richest, and richest of all on the inner rings towards [[the Gates]]; towards the docks their houses are narrower, their gardens smaller.

name: The Docks
description: The Verge's waterfront on the lough, on either side of the walled mouth of the [[Lagan Estuary]], some 400 m deep: docks dug into the shore between the mouths of the ring canals, quays and warehouses, timber yards, a rope-walk and a shipyard, and nearby the walled trading houses of the nations, each its own enclave of the free port. Most of the [[Committee Interior]]'s goods lie here and in [[the Bond]], in bond until they are declassified and dealt for. The port's labourers live among the warehouses and in the crowded courts behind them, the poorest of the Verge.

name: The Outer Verge
description: Beyond the rings, [[the Verge]] sprawls with no walls to stop it, and thins as it goes: first workshops, yards and newer, poorer streets; then merchants' villas in their gardens, market gardens and orchards that feed the city, tenter grounds where cloth dries on its hooks, rope-walks, and lanes with houses strung along them between the fields, until the city fades into the country. On its north-east side, downwind, the works that make up what is landed keep apart: sugar houses, distilleries, soap-boilers, dyers and tobacco works; and on the docks' side, close in, the poorest streets crowd, courts and alleys as close-packed as Amsterdam's Jordaan.

name: The Gates
description: Where Stora's three causeways come ashore on [[the Verge]]: the dearest ground in [[Ephemeristorum]]. The trade that crosses here is the Committee Interior's in person: delegations and their negotiators going over to [[Stora]] to deal, and the smaller, dearer goods that have been inspected in [[Ephe]] in small batches and are released through Stora. About [[the Exchange]] keep the brokers, factors, money-changers, notaries, translators and consuls' agents, in tall stone houses with gardens behind; behind them crowd the inns and lodging houses of the delegations' followers, and everyone who would hear first what was agreed. Working name.

name: The Exchange
description: At the head of Stora's middle causeway, on its square at [[the Gates]]: where the deals for the [[Committee Interior]]'s goods are struck and their prices cried, between the negotiators back from [[Stora]] and the merchants of every nation. Working name.

name: The Bond
description: Walled stores by the [[Orbital]]'s lock, on the Verge's side: where the [[Committee Interior]]'s goods in bulk lie in bond, undeclassified, until a deal is struck for them at [[the Exchange]] and they are cleared. With the hulks moored along the Orbital's outer bank, floating stores of the same, and the warehouses of [[the Docks]], they hold most of what Ephemeristorum sells: none of it need ever go into [[Ephe]]. Working name.
